Subject: Upcoming penetration test — need attack-surface mapping and scope clarifications

Hi Aditya,

We are scheduling a third-party penetration test (ThirdPath Sec) for Acme's integration with Redwood. The vendor has asked for a clear mapping of which surfaces are in-scope versus out-of-scope. Specifically they want confirmation for:

- Hosted (Redwood API, public endpoints) — do you consider this in-scope?
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools hosted by Redwood for Acme) — which host/network boundaries apply?
- Private/VPC (customer VPC connectors) — are these customer-managed or Redwood-managed for the purposes of testing?
- On-prem deployments (if any) — are there variants we should note?

Can you send a short diagram or a one-page matrix and any notes on where credentials/keys are stored, and whether simulating auth flows is permitted? Also please confirm whether Redwood will provide contact for blast-radius/containment questions during testing.

Thanks — we need this to finalize the Statement of Work (SOW) by EOD Friday.

Best,
Samantha Jones
Head of Security, Acme Corp

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming penetration test — need attack-surface mapping and scope clarifications

Samantha — thanks for the note. Quick answers up-front, and attaching a compact mapping + boundary diagram. See attachments.

Summary (high-level):
- Hosted API (Redwood public endpoints): IN SCOPE for external/network tests and API auth flows. Note: customer data in transit to hosted endpoints is part of scope for network/endpoint testing, but we will redact live customer PII on request.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): IN SCOPE for internal host-level and service-level testing, but we require testing to be non-disruptive to other tenants. We will provide an isolated test reservation or snapshot where feasible.
- Private / VPC connectors: PARTIALLY IN SCOPE. If the deployment is Redwood-managed (customer uses Redwood Private hosted in their VPC with Redwood control plane access), we cover our control plane components and connectors. If the customer manages the compute (air-gapped on-prem), then on-prem components are OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood — they fall under the customer's responsibility.
- On-prem: generally OUT OF_SCOPE for Redwood unless a specific Redwood on-prem package is under contract — in which case we will coordinate to produce a separate scope addendum.

Auth flows: You can simulate OAuth and API-key flows. For any credential-related testing we request ephemeral test creds and an agreed kill-switch.

Contacts for testing day: Kar thik Iyer (kar thik_iyer@redwood.ai) will be the technical lead; I will be the contract/coordination lead.

I attached a one-page "attack-surface mapping" PDF and a simple boundary spreadsheet — both include a recommended list of allowed tests, disallowed destructive tests, and our containment phone numbers. Let me know if you want us to open a scoped invite to ThirdPath for a pre-test walkthrough.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Manager, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_pt_scope_diagram.pdf, redwood_network_boundary.xlsx

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Clarifying Dedicated environment network access and allowed tests — answers and whitelist

Ben / Samantha — thanks, good questions. Answers and next steps below.

1) Bastion / admin hosts: Dedicated reservations get isolated admin planes; bastions are not shared across customers. We will provide a temporary admin subnet and a jump-host specifically for the test window. Lateral movement across other customers' hosts is STRICTLY prohibited and not possible from the reservation scope.

2) CIDR ranges / egress IPs: see redwood_network_boundary.xlsx (tab ‘Whitelists’) — we provide short-lived CIDRs for the test window and a list of egress IPs for management traffic. For the VPC connectors where Redwood runs the control plane, those control-plane IPs are included. If Acme is operating customer-managed compute in their VPC, we will not provide those ranges.

3) Multi-tenant management endpoints: excluded endpoints are listed in the attached diagram (acme_pt_scope_diagram.pdf) and summarized here: /internal-admin, /billing/*, and internal telemetry ingestion endpoints. Please do not target those.

Containment & Kill-switch: Kar thik (cc'd) will be on-call during the window and can cut network access to the reservation. Contact: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai / +1 415 555 0199.

We are available for the 30-minute walkthrough Thu 26 Feb 10:00 PT — confirmed. After the call we will share ephemeral creds and the final SOW for signature.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Manager, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference
